summary: Latency regression: p95/p99 spikes and occasional request timeouts tied to continuous batching
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NebulaPay reports intermittent high tail latency (p95/p99) and occasional request timeouts (504) beginning after the last runtime deploy. Spikes observed primarily on text-generation endpoints that use continuous batching.

Impact:
- Multiple requests experiencing p95 latency regression from ~120ms to ~900-1,200ms; p99 up to ~2,500ms.
- Roughly 2.4% of requests for the customer returned 504/timeouts during spike windows.
- Affects production traffic for NebulaPay (dedicated capacity) and a small fraction of hosted customers in us-east.

Environment:
- prod | us-east (primary), eu-west (secondary)
- Serving runtime: 2026-02-18 release (runtime v3.8.1)
- Scheduler: continuous-batching enabled with batch_wait_ms default change in recent deploy
- Models involved: redwood-13B-v1, redwood-7B-q4_0

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1. Send steady mixed-length generation traffic at ~8-12 QPS with bursts to the /v1/generate endpoint pinned to redwood-13B-v1.
2. Observe tail latencies reported in client telemetry and on the dashboard.
3. Reproduce more easily by adding occasional single-shot long-sequence requests (seq_len ~2048) interspersed with short requests.

Observed metrics / logs:
- p95 latency (hosted route) jumped from ~120ms baseline to 900-1,200ms starting 2026-02-19 04:00 UTC.
- p99 latency peaked at ~2.4s for the same period.
- Continuous-batching queue length metric shows increased wait times: mean batch_hold_time increased from 12ms -> 180ms during spike windows.
- Autoscaling metrics: no GPU scale event triggered during some spike windows; CPU/memory under typical utilization for the node pool.
- Request logs show increased "wait_for_batch_ms" durations and several caller-side timeouts (504) correlated with long batch hold times.

Initial hypothesis:
- Change in continuous batching defaults in runtime v3.8.1 increased batch_wait_ms or introduced backoff behavior causing longer batch collection times under low-but-bursty traffic patterns.
- When sequence-length variance is high, batch shaping causes a few long requests to delay batch dispatch, amplifying tail latency for short requests.
- Scheduler and serving-runtime interaction (kernel selection path) may be delaying dispatch for certain model variants, especially quantized paths (7B q4).
comments: 2026-02-20 Sophie Chen: Customer opened ticket after observing p99 spikes and several 504s. Shared client telemetry and request IDs. Escalated to SRE oncall.

2026-02-20 Ravi Patel: Acknowledged. Reproducing against a repro harness in our staging cluster with continuous-batching toggled. Initial logs point to batch_hold_time jumps after the recent runtime deploy.
2026-02-21 Sophie Chen: Customer confirmed that pinning model to redwood-7B-q4_0 reduced 504 rate but did not eliminate p99 spikes. They provided request IDs and traffic patterns.

2026-02-21 Ravi Patel: Ran microbenchmarks. When batch_wait_ms is at 150-200ms we see higher p95/p99 for mixed seq_len traffic; when it's 15-30ms tail returns to baseline. Filing a follow-up with runtime team to check default change in v3.8.1.

2026-02-22 Lina Gomez (Runtime Eng): Noted a change in default batching backoff introduced in commit 7f3a2b1 that increases batch_wait_ms adaptively to reduce CPU churn. We'll validate if backoff triggers incorrectly for dedicated nodes with lower QPS.

2026-02-23 Ravi Patel: Deployed a canary rollback of batching-defaults on a single pool (canary-pool-7) for NebulaPay. Preliminary metrics show p95 down to ~180ms and p99 below 600ms for the canary. No regressions observed in throughput.
2026-02-24 Sophie Chen: Customer confirmed improved latency on canary pool, willing to accept temporary routing to canary as workaround while we prepare a fix.

2026-02-25 Ravi Patel: Coordinate next steps with runtime release. Plan to ship runtime patch that restores previous batch_wait baseline and add a new flag to tune adaptive backoff per-customer. Need release window and rollout plan.
investigation_notes: Reproduction: Created traffic generator that mimics NebulaPay mix (8-12 QPS, 5-10% long seq requests). Observed replicate of p99 spikes only when continuous batching adaptive backoff enabled.
Metric correlation: batch_hold_time and batch_size variance correlate strongly with tail latency. Longer hold times align with p99 windows.
Code pointer: commit 7f3a2b1 in scheduler introduced adaptive backoff increase logic. Suspected mis-calibration for dedicated pools with smaller request footprints.
Canary test: Rolling back adaptive backoff on canary-pool-7 reduced tail significantly without affecting throughput or increasing CPU by more than 3%.
Edge cases: Requests that exceed model-specific kernel-selection thresholds (long sequences) still contribute to batch shaping; consider per-model backoff defaults.
Risk assessment: Rolling back adaptive backoff is low risk for short-term mitigation; long-term fix should add per-pool/per-customer tuning knobs and better heuristics for mixed-length traffic.
resolution_notes:
Workaround implemented: rerouted NebulaPay traffic to canary pool with adaptive backoff disabled (2026-02-23). This reduced p95/p99 to near-baseline while we prepare an official fix.
Planned fix: runtime patch to adjust adaptive backoff thresholds and expose per-pool config (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2158). Target release: 2026-02-27 canary, 2026-03-01 global rollout behind feature flag.
Follow-ups: add an automated test in CI that simulates mixed-sequence-length traffic to detect future regressions; add dashboard alert for batch_hold_time exceeding 100ms for >5m.
next_steps: Finalize runtime patch and open PR for review (assigned to Lina Gomez)
Schedule canary rollout 2026-02-27 and monitor p95/p99, batch_hold_time, and request timeout rate
Communicate temporary routing/workaround to NebulaPay and provide postmortem once fix is rolled out
